To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ImageNet Pretrained models can be used to initialize audio classification models, (2) the performance variance is due to random initialization and random mini batch ordering, (3) an ensemble of ImageNet models with diverse initialization can achieve state-of-the-art results on audio classification tasks.
ImageNet pretrained CNN models can be successfully applied to audio spectrogram classification tasks, even though there are significant differences between the image and the spectrogram data.
ImageNet pretrained CNNs can be used as a strong baseline network for audio classification.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How well can we transfer ImageNet pretrained models for audio classification?

the following questions: (1) What are the best CNN architectures for audio classification? (2) What makes a good CNN model for audio classification? and (3) How can we build better ensembles with CNNs for audio classification?.
the following questions: (1) Can we use ImageNet pretrained CNN models for audio classification?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ImageNet Pretraining works for audio classification and can be a strong baseline model to start with.
CNNs are very good at learning spectrogram representations and ImageNet pretraining is a very good way to initialize the weights for the task.
the ImageNet pretrained standard CNNs are a strong baseline for audio classification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ImageNet pretrained CNN models are a strong baseline for audio classification.
the ImageNet pretrained CNN models can be a strong baseline network for audio classification and can be used to achieve state of the art results.
ImageNet pretrained models can be used to learn useful audio representation and that ensemble of these models can achieve state of the art performance on ESC-50 and UrbanSound8K datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ImageNet pretrained CNN models can be directly used to learn audio classification models with only minor modifications to the input and output layer.
standard ImageNet pretrained CNNs can be used as a good starting point for audio classification.
ImageNet pretrained standard models can be used to learn audio representations and can be used as a strong baseline model for audio classification.
